source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 is a 114 MW, 685,000 square foot data center in Sterling, Virginia, the third largest by published IT capacity among the 25 Virginia facilities that disclose megawatt figures.

The published capacity is the useful number, not the rack math. At 114 MW the campus is sized for accelerator-dense workloads, and at 8 GPUs per rack the operator's own reading puts it near 2,280 high-end accelerators. That is a single building's worth of training or serving capacity, and it sits in Ashburn, inside Northern Virginia's existing power and network backbone rather than at the edge of it.

The scale only reads as large against what Virginia discloses. The state's 330 mapped data centers publish 1,603 MW combined, so this one campus is 7.1 percent of the disclosed total. Most mapped facilities publish nothing, which means the real state load is substantially larger and this share is a floor, not a ranking of true capacity.

What the data does not cover is the constraint that matters most. No interconnection queue position, no power purchase agreement, no substation capacity, and no expansion timeline is published here. A 114 MW nameplate says what the building was designed to draw, not what the grid has agreed to deliver or when.
